set.body:
OWNER DIRECTION: REVISIT FILM. Open data is strongest there. It must be COHERENT, MODULAR, AND
BUILD ON WHAT WE HAVE. Write the ADR.

THE SEAM IS NARROWER THAN THE FILE COUNT SUGGESTS, and I measured it rather than estimating:

  AlignmentSource.sourceSupport(target): Option[SpanSet]   story/alignment.scala:43   LOCATOR seam
  SourceView.textLength: Int                               align/source.scala:144     DENOMINATOR seam

SpanSet appears in 48 files across 14 modules, but MOST OF THOSE ARE TEXT-SIDE AND STAY TEXT-SIDE.
What must generalise is the ALIGNMENT-SIDE CONTRACT, and that is two members in traits. Traits are
cheap to generalise; 48 concrete uses are not, and we do not have to.

SurfaceAtlas is a `final class ... private` (core/atlas.scala:160). Do NOT unseal it -- sweep 2
closed that construction boundary today. A trait ABOVE it is purely additive.

WHAT REUSES WHAT WE BUILT, and this is the argument for doing it now rather than later:

  THE COMPILER GENERALISES. document takes atlas + typed proposals + evidence -> NarrativeCompilation.
  FOR FILM, THE ANNOTATION IS THE PROPOSAL SOURCE. Four call sites take SurfaceAtlas concretely;
  they take the trait instead. The compiler itself does not change.

  THE CLAIM SYSTEM IS ALREADY THE RIGHT SHAPE. An annotation is NATIVELY a proposal with a receipt
  from somebody else's coding pass. DerivationReceipt, epistemic status, provenance and the
  proposal/observation distinction were built for exactly this and currently have only one
  consumer.

  EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM OF NarrativeGraph IS UNTOUCHED: alignment, the cost model, supportWeight,
  eligibility, RecallGraph, signature. The recall side is TEXT whatever the source medium is.

WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW:

  PresentationAxis CARRYING ITS KIND. textLength becomes axis.extent; positions become
  RelativePosition[axis.Kind] so a character offset and a PTS FAIL TO COMPILE rather than failing a
  runtime check. new-engineer proposed the path-dependent shape and it is the right one.
  A Support abstraction with a kind: SpanSet is the text implementation, an interval set is the
  film one.
  A Sherlock ingest adapter.

THE LIMIT THE AUDIT FORCES US TO STATE, and it goes in the ADR rather than being discovered:
e022c5f found the released annotations supply ordering, 50 scene markers, 1000 microsegments,
character presence/focus/speaker, location and sensory features -- BUT NO RELATIONS OR ROLES, no
dialogue propositions, and no situation IDs or contexts. A film NarrativeGraph built from them
will be SPARSE: situations and ordering, few relations. That constrains what film alignment can
measure and it must be said up front.

SEQUENCING, AND FILM DOES NOT JUMP THE QUEUE: the recall side is text, and the annotation's
narrative-description field needs the SAME extraction to become propositions. Stage 1b
(bd-01M17MET0E4TWW304YKXPHBSBG) serves BOTH sides. Film reuses that bottleneck twice rather than
avoiding it once. Anyone proposing film as a route around the provider has the dependency
backwards.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: the ADR only. Name the two trait seams, the axis type, the Support
abstraction, the atlas trait, the four compiler call sites, and the sparseness limit. NO CODE.
root holds the film-source-representation topic and the locator/denominator/absence-erasing
classification; this is the concrete migration shape that follows from it plus tonight's Sherlock
measurement.

Unassigned. Whoever takes it: the classification work is root's and the Sherlock capability table
is collab's -- build on both rather than re-deriving.
set.title: ADR: film as a source -- two trait seams, a typed presentation axis, and what stays untouched
